operations.name: fetch_ndvi
operations.description: Sentinel-2 for the AOI. `product: "ndvi"` (default) returns cloud-masked NDVI vegetation statistics plus a red→yellow→green NDVI raster layer — use it for NDVI stats AND for any "show/colorize/map NDVI" visualization request. `product: "imagery"` returns the 10 m true-colour RGB scene instead.

product.description: ndvi (default) = NDVI statistics + colormap raster; imagery = true-colour RGB.

limitations: Uses the clearest recent Sentinel-2 L2A scene over the AOI, not a composite; Sentinel-2 data begins 2015-06-23.
Cloud, shadow and cirrus are masked with the scene classification (SCL) layer; masked pixels are excluded from the statistics, not filled.
The mean is read from a grid capped at 256 px, so over a large AOI its effective ground sample distance is coarser than 10 m (the output states it).
If tiles cannot be rendered the map shows a flat fill derived from the real mean, labelled illustrative, or nothing when no mean exists.
operations.confidence: high: a clear scene (at least 40% of AOI pixels clear) with rendered per-pixel tiles; medium or low when cloud, a flat fallback fill or a composite limits it.

operations.name: compute_spectral_index
operations.description: Compute a spectral index from Sentinel-2 bands with its default styling. Supports NDVI, NDWI, NDBI, EVI, NBR, SAVI. For a custom colormap, stretch, sensor or date window, use render_raster with the index formula as `expression`.
limitations: Sentinel-2 L2A only; fixed default colormap and a stretch fitted to the AOI's own p2-p98 (use render_raster for anything custom).
Cloud, shadow and cirrus are masked with the SCL layer before the mean is computed.
The mean comes from a grid capped at 256 px, so its effective resolution over a large AOI is coarser than 10 m.
operations.confidence: high: a clear scene with rendered tiles; medium when cloud or a flat fallback fill limits it.

operations.name: fetch_temporal_stack
operations.description: Fetch a time series of NDVI data across multiple months for temporal analysis.

months.description: Number of months to look back (default 6, max 12)

limitations: One cloud-masked NDVI mean per clear acquisition; dates with no usable clear-sky value are absent, never interpolated.
At most 12 months back; each point is a single scene, so the series is irregular in time.
operations.confidence: medium: depends on how many clear acquisitions exist in the window; fewer than three points is a weak trend.

operations.name: fetch_thermal
operations.description: Fetch Land Surface Temperature (LST) from Landsat 9 thermal data for the AOI.
limitations: Landsat 8/9 Collection 2 Level 2 surface temperature (acquired about 10:30 local time), so a daytime snapshot, not a daily mean.
Needs a clear-sky scene; the thermal band is resampled to 30 m from a coarser native resolution.
Land surface temperature, not air temperature, and not fire detection.
operations.confidence: high: a clear Landsat scene over the AOI; medium or low with partial cloud or a coarser fallback source.

operations.name: fetch_sar
operations.description: Fetch Sentinel-1 SAR (Synthetic Aperture Radar) backscatter data for the AOI. SAR sees through clouds and detects flood extent, urban structure, and surface roughness. Returns VV-band amplitude statistics and a false-color radar image. Use for flood mapping, change detection, or when cloud cover blocks optical sensors.
limitations: Sentinel-1 GRD VV backscatter amplitude: an image of surface roughness and moisture, not a flood product (use map_flood for floods).
Radar geometry distorts steep terrain (layover, shadow) and speckle is not filtered.
operations.confidence: medium: real backscatter, but interpretation (water, urban, rough surface) depends on context the radar image alone cannot give.

operations.name: fetch_surface_water
operations.description: Fetch long-term surface water history from JRC Global Surface Water v1.4 (1984–2021, 30 m). Shows water occurrence (% of years each pixel held water) derived from 37 years of Landsat data. Use for: "show water history", "is this area seasonally flooded?", "permanent vs seasonal water", "has the lake shrunk?", "floodplain mapping", "flood frequency".
limitations: JRC Global Surface Water v1.4 covers 1984-2021 only: it says nothing about recent floods or water after 2021.
Occurrence is the share of valid Landsat observations with water; cloudy or sparsely observed places carry larger uncertainty.
30 m pixels: narrow channels and small ponds are missed.
operations.confidence: high for long-term water behaviour inside 1984-2021; not applicable to current extent.

operations.name: fetch_active_fires
operations.description: Detect active wildfires and thermal anomalies from NASA FIRMS satellite data (VIIRS 375 m + MODIS 1 km NRT). Returns geolocated fire hotspots with fire radiative power (FRP in MW), acquisition time, satellite, and confidence. Use for: "are there active fires?", "wildfire monitoring", "show fire hotspots", "thermal anomalies from fire", "burning areas". Requires FIRMS_MAP_KEY env var (free at firms.modaps.eosdis.nasa.gov/api/area/); gracefully explains how to get the key if absent.

days.description: Look-back window in days (1–10, default 7). Use 1–2 for currently active fires; 7–10 for recent fire history.

limitations: NASA FIRMS near-real-time hotspots: each point is a thermal anomaly in a 375 m (VIIRS) or 1 km (MODIS) pixel, not a measured fire perimeter.
Requires a free FIRMS_MAP_KEY; without it the tool says so and returns nothing.
Look-back window is 1-10 days; clouds and satellite overpass times mean fires can be missed.
operations.confidence: per-hotspot: the FIRMS confidence class (low / nominal / high) reported with each detection.

operations.name: fetch_built_surface
operations.description: Measure built-up surface coverage using ESA WorldCover 2021 (10 m Sentinel-2 derived, via Planetary Computer STAC, free, no key). Returns built-up %, tree cover %, cropland %, grassland %, water %, and dominant land class for the AOI. Renders a categorical LULC raster layer with 11-class coloring. Use for: "how urban/built-up is this area?", "impervious surface fraction", "built-up area", "urban footprint", "what percentage is developed?", "land cover from satellite".
limitations: ESA WorldCover 2021 is a single year; it does not show change since 2021.
A 10 m land-cover classification (about 75% overall accuracy globally): built-up % is a classification share, not a surveyed impervious area.
operations.confidence: medium: a published global product with documented accuracy, applied without local validation.

operations.name: render_raster
operations.description: Display ANY band, band composite or band-math expression of a Sentinel-2 L2A or Landsat C2 L2 scene over the AOI as a map layer (masked to the drawn polygon, stretched to the AOI's own p2–p98). Use for "show the NIR band", "false colour B08/B04/B03", "SWIR composite", "show (B11-B08)/(B11+B08)". Pass `bands` (1 = single-band colormap, 3 = RGB composite) OR `expression`. Unknown bands return an error naming the valid ones — never substitute another band or index.

sensor.description: Default sentinel-2-l2a. Sentinel-2 bands: B01-B09, B8A, B11, B12 (or blue/green/red/nir/swir16/swir22). Landsat bands: coastal, blue, green, red, nir08, swir16, swir22.

bands.description: 1 band or 3 bands in R,G,B order, e.g. ["B08","B04","B03"] for false colour.

expression.description: Band math over band names with + - * / and parentheses, e.g. "(B11-B08)/(B11+B08)". Evaluated on surface reflectance.

date.description: YYYY-MM-DD; the clearest scene within +-3 days is used.

start.description: YYYY-MM-DD window start (default: 90 days before end).

colormap.description: Single band / expression only: viridis (default), magma, inferno, plasma, cividis, greys, rdylgn, rdbu, spectral, terrain, blues, ylgn (append _r to reverse).

rescale.description: [min, max] display stretch. Omit to use the AOI p2–p98. Single band/expression: reflectance or index units; RGB: raw DN.

limitations: Shows exactly the band, composite or expression asked for; an unknown band is refused, never replaced by another product.
The default stretch is the p2-p98 of the AOI's own clear pixels, so colours are relative to this AOI, not comparable between AOIs.
Sentinel-2 data begins 2015-06-23; Landsat Collection 2 begins 1982-08-22. Landsat is 30 m, Sentinel-2 10-20 m depending on the band.
If no scene reaches the clear-sky floor the newest scene is shown unmasked and flagged.
operations.confidence: high: a clear scene (at least 80% of AOI pixels clear) with a measured stretch; medium otherwise; low when the only scene available is cloudy and unmasked.

operations.name: analyze_raster
operations.description: ONE parameterised analysis capability over real, polygon-clipped, cloud-masked Sentinel-2 pixels. Pick an `operation` and pass its parameters — this is how the agent answers a SPECIFIC analytical request rather than only pre-wired ones. Operations: `stats` (mean/median/σ/percentiles); `histogram` (distribution shape; `bins`, `range`); `variogram` (spatial structure and ANISOTROPY — `lag_m` bin width in metres, `max_lag_m`, `direction_deg` azimuth 0=N/90=E, `tolerance_deg`, `model`; fits nugget/sill/range); `transect` (profile along a user-supplied `line`); `correlate` (relationship between `index` and `index2` on one scene — e.g. NDVI vs NDBI); `texture` (local heterogeneity; `window` px, `metric` stddev|range|mad); `cluster` (unsupervised zonation; `k`, `indices`); `change` (per-pixel delta between `date` and `date2`, masked on BOTH dates). Every operation uses only clear pixels (SCL cloud/shadow/cirrus masked) inside the drawn polygon. Use for: "variogram", "directional variogram", "semivariogram", "spatial autocorrelation", "how patchy", "correlation length", "distribution of NDVI", "profile along this line", "is NDVI related to built-up", "how rough is the surface", "zone this field", "percentiles".

date.description: Target date YYYY-MM-DD; the clearest scene within ±30 days is used. For `change`, this is the BEFORE date.

lag_m.description: Variogram lag-bin WIDTH in metres (e.g. 40). Must be ≥ the pixel size.

max_lag_m.description: Largest variogram lag in metres (default: half the AOI diagonal).

direction_deg.description: Variogram azimuth: 0 = north, 90 = east. Omit for omnidirectional.

model.description: Variogram model to fit (default auto — best RMSE).

window.description: Texture window size in pixels, odd, ≥3 (default 3).

threshold.description: Change magnitude counted as real movement (default 0.05).

bracket.description: `change` only: take the BEFORE scene from the 45 days up to `date` and the AFTER scene from the 45 days from `date2`, instead of the clearest scene within ±30 days of each. Use it when an event happened somewhere between the two dates, so neither scene can fall after (or before) it.

baseline_min.description: `change` only: count only pixels whose `index` on the BEFORE date was at least this, e.g. NBR 0.15 to measure burn change on vegetated ground only. The result reports the share of the area this keeps; fewer than 30 pixels is refused as too few.

max_size.description: Longest-edge pixel budget, 32–512 (default 256). Raise for finer lags on a large AOI.

limitations: Every operation uses only clear pixels (SCL cloud, shadow and cirrus masked) inside the drawn polygon.
Pixel budget is capped (default 256, maximum 512 on the longest edge), so over a large AOI the grid is coarser than 10 m.
Variogram lags below the pixel size are refused; change detection masks pixels cloudy on either date.
operations.confidence: high when many clear pixels support the statistic; the result reports the clear-pixel count so thin support is visible.

operations.name: inspect_imagery
operations.description: LOOK at the AOI: render it from real Sentinel-2 pixels and have a vision model describe what is actually visible, then place that description next to the SCL cloud numbers for the same scene. Use this to sanity-check a statistic against the picture — cloud, haze, snow, sensor artefact, water — or to answer "what am I looking at here?" and "does this number make sense?". The true-colour view is deliberately NOT cloud-masked, so cloud is visible rather than removed. Requires a vision-capable model (VLM_ENDPOINT + VLM_MODEL, or an OpenAI/Claude/Gemini key in Settings); when none is configured it says so and describes nothing.

subject.description: What to render: true colour (default) or a spectral index map.

index.description: Index to render when subject is "index".

question.description: A specific question about the picture (e.g. "is this area under cloud?").

date.description: Target date YYYY-MM-DD; a scene within ±30 days is used.

scene.description: "clearest" (default) inspects the same scene the statistics used; "newest" inspects the latest acquisition regardless of cloud — the right choice for "is it cloudy right now?".

limitations: Needs a vision-capable model (VLM_ENDPOINT + VLM_MODEL, or an OpenAI / Claude / Gemini key in Settings); with none configured it describes nothing.
The true-colour view is deliberately not cloud-masked, so cloud stays visible.
A description is an interpretation of a picture at 10 m, not a measurement.
operations.confidence: low to medium: a vision model's reading of the image, shown beside the measured cloud numbers for the same scene.

operations.name: composite
operations.description: Cloud-FREE Sentinel-2 composite for a date window: the per-pixel MEDIAN of every clear observation (cloud, shadow and cirrus masked per pixel) between `start` and `end`, shown as a map layer with the real p2–p98 range. Use for "cloud-free", "median", "seasonal / monthly / growing-season average", "best available picture of September", or any window where a single scene would be cloudy or unrepresentative. Pass an `expression` (NDVI, NDWI, NDBI, EVI, NBR, SAVI, or band math such as "(B11-B08)/(B11+B08)") OR `bands` (1 band, or 3 in R,G,B order). The result is NOT one acquisition date: it reports how many scenes and clear observations per pixel it rests on. For a specific day use fetch_ndvi / render_raster instead.

expression.description: A named index (NDVI, NDWI, NDBI, EVI, NBR, SAVI) or band math over Sentinel-2 bands with + - * / and parentheses, e.g. "(B08-B04)/(B08+B04)". The index is computed on the median reflectance.

bands.description: 1 band (single-band map) or 3 bands in R,G,B order, e.g. ["B04","B03","B02"] for a true-colour composite. Use instead of `expression`.

start.description: YYYY-MM-DD window start (default: 30 days before end). The window may span at most 366 days.

colormap.description: Single band / expression only: rdylgn (default for indices), viridis (default otherwise), magma, inferno, plasma, cividis, greys, rdbu, spectral, terrain, blues, ylgn (append _r to reverse).

rescale.description: [min, max] display stretch for a single band / expression. Omit to use the composite's own p2–p98.

resolution.description: Pixel size in metres, 10–100 (default 10). Raise it for a large AOI.

max_cloud.description: Optional scene-level cloud-cover ceiling in % (pixels are masked regardless). Omit unless the user asks.

limitations: A median of the clear observations in the window, not an acquisition: change inside the window (harvest, flood, burn) is blended, and the result carries no single date.

Cloud, shadow, cirrus, saturated and "dark area" pixels are masked per pixel with the SCL layer, so very dark surfaces can be under-represented; a pixel with no clear observation stays empty, never filled.

A window of at most 366 days and an AOI of at most 2,500 km² (25 million pixels at 10 m); a long window over a large AOI can still exceed the service's memory cap, which is reported, not truncated; Sentinel-2 L2A only, data from 2015-06-23.
The first call for a new window takes tens of seconds (it reads every scene); an identical repeat is served from the service cache.
operations.confidence: high: at least 90% of the AOI has a clear observation and every pixel has at least 3; medium at 60% valid and 3 clear observations on average; low otherwise (the median is then close to a single, possibly unrepresentative, date).

operations.name: detect_anomaly
operations.description: Is a given month UNUSUAL for this area? Forecasts the index for `month` from the preceding years of monthly Sentinel-2 history (default 5), then compares it with the OBSERVED value for that month. Returns observed, expected median and 80% range (p10 to p90), and a verdict: within_expected, below_expected, above_expected or cannot_determine (no clear observation that month, or history too short or sparse). Use for "is this September greener/browner than normal", "was vegetation unusual in <month>", "expected vs observed NDVI". The expected value is a forecast; say so and quote the range.

month.description: YYYY-MM, the month to judge. Must not be in the future; the current month is judged on the scenes so far.

expression.description: Index: NDVI, NDWI, NDBI, EVI, NBR, SAVI (default NDVI) or band math.

history_years.description: Years of history before the month used for the expectation, 3-10 (default 5).

limitations: Forecast, not observation: the expected values are extrapolated from past seasonality of the same area; they say what the history makes likely, not what happened or will happen. Drought, flooding, harvest timing, a land-use change or a trend break leave the range.

The series is the spatial median over the AOI of a cloud-masked monthly composite (Sentinel-2 L2A). A month counts as observed only if at least 30% of the AOI had a clear observation; gaps of at most 2 months are linearly interpolated and flagged, longer gaps are left open, and the operation refuses with fewer than 36 months of history, more than 25% missing months, or no clear observation in the last 2 months.

Monthly cadence, an AOI of at most 100 km², history from 2017-01 (earlier scenes are not readable); the first call for an area reads years of scenes and can take minutes, a repeat is served from cache.
A mixed AOI (field plus town, forest plus crop) is summarised by one median, which can hide opposite changes inside it.

The verdict compares one observed month against a 80% range, so about 1 month in 5 falls outside it by chance; "below" or "above" is a flag to look closer, not a diagnosis of drought, damage or change.
operations.confidence: medium: the shipped method's p10-p90 range held the observed value 70-90% of the time on the backtest (eval/RESULTS.md) AND at most 10% of the history months were interpolated; low otherwise (no backtest, miscalibrated, or gappy input). Never high: it is a forecast. The percentage reported is measured backtest coverage across the backtest AOIs, not a guarantee for this one.

operations.name: fetch_dem
operations.description: Fetch Digital Elevation Model (DEM) from Mapzen ~30m (global merged) data (opentopodata.org) for the AOI. Returns elevation statistics.
limitations: The source and its resolution depend on the configured elevation endpoint (the description names it); it is a surface model, not a survey.
Statistics come from a sampled grid over the AOI, not every DEM cell.
Vertical error of a global DEM is several metres, larger in steep or forested terrain.
operations.confidence: medium: a published global DEM sampled over the AOI; it does not know local surveying error.

operations.name: fetch_elevation_derivatives
operations.description: Compute slope (%), aspect (compass bearing), and/or elevation contour lines from the existing DEM grid (same source as fetch_dem) — no new data fetch required. Use for: "how steep is this?", "show me the slope", "north or south-facing?", "aspect map", "draw contours", "topographic contours", "contour lines every Xm", "is this flat or hilly?", "where are the steep slopes?", "which way does the land face?", "elevation profile".

kind.description: Which derivatives to compute. "all" (default) returns slope raster + aspect raster + contour lines as three separate layers.

contour_interval.description: Contour interval in meters (default: auto-selected based on terrain relief — 5/10/25/50/100 m). Minimum 5 m.

limitations: Derived from the same DEM grid as fetch_dem, at that grid's resolution: macro-scale terrain, not metre-scale roughness.
Slope and aspect are undefined on flat ground and unreliable at the grid edge; contours are interpolated.
operations.confidence: medium: inherits the DEM's vertical error, which dominates slope on gentle terrain.

operations.name: fetch_weather_history
operations.description: Fetch historical weather data from ERA5 reanalysis for the AOI.
limitations: ERA5 reanalysis at the AOI centroid on a roughly 25 km grid: a regional climate signal, not a station measurement.
Monthly summary of the last year; no rainy-season or climatology framing (use fetch_precipitation_history for that).
operations.confidence: medium: a well-validated reanalysis, coarse relative to the AOI.

operations.name: fetch_precipitation_history
operations.description: Fetch 30-year monthly precipitation climatology (ERA5 1991–2020 reference period) and last 24 months of anomalies for the AOI centroid. Optionally adds a CHIRPS monthly rainfall raster layer to the map. Use for: "is it getting drier here?", "rainfall history", "precipitation history", "rainy season", "when does it rain?", "drought", "wet year", "dry year", "annual rainfall", "monthly rainfall", "how much rain falls here?", "climate trend", "rainfall anomaly", "below-average rain", "monsoon timing". Answers questions about whether recent rainfall is above or below the 30-year average.

months_back.description: How many recent months to include in the anomaly table (default: 24, max: 60).

include_raster.description: Whether to fetch a CHIRPS monthly rainfall raster and add it to the map (default: true). Set to false for stats-only output.

limitations: The climatology and anomalies are an ERA5 grid cell at the AOI centroid (about 25 km), labelled clip "centroid"; they can miss local or orographic variation.
Anomalies compare recent months to the 1991-2020 reference period.
The CHIRPS raster trails the present by about 2-3 months.
operations.confidence: medium: reanalysis-based; direction of an anomaly is more reliable than its size.

operations.name: query_osm
operations.description: Query OpenStreetMap for objects and infrastructure within the AOI. Returns GeoJSON features with correct geometry types: rivers/roads as LineStrings, buildings/farms/orchards as Polygons. If no results found, suggests using computer vision.
limitations: OpenStreetMap records what volunteers have mapped, not everything that exists: zero results can mean "not mapped".
Dense areas are fetched in quadrants; a still-saturated quadrant is reported as truncated and the count is then a lower bound.
operations.confidence: high when the query completed for every quadrant; medium when quadrants were truncated or failed (the output says which).

operations.name: query_3d_tiles
operations.description: Fetch building footprints with height data from OpenStreetMap for the AOI. Heights are derived from explicit tags, floor-count estimates, or type defaults. Returns colored polygons with height, levels, and building type. Use for urban density, skyline analysis, or building inventory requests.
limitations: Building heights come from explicit OSM tags, floor-count estimates (levels x 3.5 m) or type defaults, so many are estimates.
Only buildings mapped in OSM; unmapped buildings are absent.
operations.confidence: medium: footprints are as complete as OSM; heights are partly estimated.

operations.name: classify_land_cover
operations.description: Classify the dominant land cover types in the AOI using Sentinel-2 NDVI fused with OSM landuse tags. Returns classes sorted by coverage percentage. Use when the user asks about "land cover", "land use", "what is this area", or "what type of land".
limitations: A coarse classification from a Sentinel-2 NDVI histogram fused with OSM landuse tags: a handful of classes, not a trained land-cover model.
Where OSM landuse is unmapped, classes rest on NDVI alone and cannot separate, for example, cropland from grassland.
operations.confidence: medium: class shares are measured from NDVI, the labels are heuristic.

operations.name: detect_change
operations.description: Detect land-cover change between two Sentinel-2 scenes. By default the latest scene against one 6-12 months earlier; with `before` / `after` dates, any two dates (use them whenever the question states a period). Returns NDVI delta, change direction (increase/decrease/stable), and magnitude. Use when the user asks about "change", "change detection", "before and after", "what changed", or "compare seasons".

before.description: YYYY-MM-DD of the earlier (baseline) state; scenes within ~30 days of it are used. For a question about a stated period, give a date at the START of that period. Omit for the default baseline.

after.description: YYYY-MM-DD of the later state; scenes within ~30 days of it are used. For a question about a stated period, give a date at the END of that period, in the same season as `before`. Omit for the latest imagery.

limitations: Compares two single Sentinel-2 scenes (by default the latest vs one 6-12 months earlier, or the dates given): seasonal change (crop cycle, leaf-off) is indistinguishable from permanent change.
NDVI delta only: it shows vegetation change, not what caused it.
operations.confidence: medium: two clear scenes give a real delta; with fewer clear pixels the delta is weaker.

operations.name: detect_deforestation
operations.description: Detect deforestation by comparing a forested baseline against a later Sentinel-2 NDVI. By default 1-2 years ago against the latest imagery; with `before` / `after` dates, any two dates (use them whenever the question states a period, e.g. a claim about 2020 to 2023). Returns deforestation flag, alert level (none/low/medium/high), and forest cover change percentage. Use when the user asks about "deforestation", "forest loss", "tree cover", or "logging".

before.description: YYYY-MM-DD of the earlier (baseline) state; scenes within ~45 days of it are used. For a question about a stated period, give a date at the START of that period. Omit for the default baseline.

after.description: YYYY-MM-DD of the later state; scenes within ~45 days of it are used. For a question about a stated period, give a date at the END of that period, in the same season as `before`. Omit for the latest imagery.

limitations: Compares a baseline (by default 1-2 years ago, or the date given) with a later Sentinel-2 NDVI (by default the latest, or the date given); it cannot tell logging from a drought, fire or harvest.
The alert level is a threshold on NDVI loss, a screening signal and not a forest-cover survey.
operations.confidence: medium: real two-epoch NDVI comparison; the alert level is heuristic.

operations.name: classify_vegetation
operations.description: Classify the functional vegetation type for the AOI — the honest answer to "what kind of trees/vegetation is this?" Combines ESA WorldCover 2021 land cover + NDVI (from GEE when configured, else WorldCover) + optional Prithvi-EO-2.0 foundation model classification (when INFERENCE_PROVIDER is set). Always honest about resolution: at 10 m Sentinel-2, returns functional type (broadleaf/needleleaf, canopy density, NDVI) — NEVER species. Species ID requires sub-meter or hyperspectral imagery. Use when asked: "what kind of trees", "what vegetation is this", "forest type", "what crops are growing", "vegetation analysis", "land cover type".
limitations: At 10 m the honest answer is functional type (broadleaf / needleleaf, canopy density, NDVI), never species; species needs sub-metre or hyperspectral imagery.
ESA WorldCover is a single year (2021).
operations.confidence: medium: WorldCover class plus measured NDVI; resolution-limited by design.

operations.name: vectorize_raster
operations.description: Digitize ANYTHING expressible from Sentinel-2 imagery into polygons: threshold a spectral index or band expression on real, cloud-masked, polygon-clipped 10 m pixels and trace the result as GeoJSON polygons (area_m2 and mean value per polygon, total area, honest resolution note). Use for "digitize all water bodies" (NDWI > 0.2), "map burn scars" (NBR < -0.1), "polygons where NDVI > 0.6", built-up (NDBI > 0.1), dense vegetation. Do NOT use for field/parcel mapping (use delineate_fields) or for objects like cars/buildings (detect_objects).

index.description: Spectral index to threshold. Give this OR expression.

expression.description: Band-name expression instead of an index, e.g. "(nir - red) / (nir + red)" or "swir16 / nir". Bands: blue green red rededge1-3 nir nir08 swir16 swir22.

op.description: Comparison. Defaults to the usual one for the index (NDWI >, NBR <, NDVI >).

threshold.description: Threshold (lower bound for "between"). A default is used for a bare index, and stated.

date.description: YYYY-MM-DD target date; the clearest scene within ±30 days is used. Omit for the latest clear scene.

min_area_m2.description: Drop polygons smaller than this (default 500 m²).

limitations: Thresholds a spectral index or band expression on cloud-masked 10 m pixels and traces the result: polygons are pixel-aligned and objects under about 100 m2 are not resolved.
A default threshold for a bare index is a starting point, and the output says so.
Not for fields or parcels (use delineate_fields) or objects such as cars and buildings.
operations.confidence: medium: the pixels are measured; whether the threshold means "water" or "burn scar" is an interpretation.

operations.name: delineate_fields
operations.description: Delineate EVERY agricultural field in the AOI as polygons, labelled by seasonal behaviour. Builds a season of cloud-masked Sentinel-2 NDVI (up to max_scenes clear dates spread over the year), segments it with a multi-temporal watershed, and labels each polygon by NDVI phenology: winter (rabi) crop, summer (kharif) crop, double-cropped, perennial/orchard, fallow/sparse, non-field. Returns area_ha, NDVI profile, peak dates, growing seasons and a 0-1 confidence per polygon. Use for "map the fields/farms/parcels/plots", "field boundaries", "how many fields", "delineate croplands". It does NOT identify crop species (wheat/rice need ground truth) and says so. Sentinel-2 10 m: reliable down to ~0.5-1 ha; adjacent same-crop fields with no visible boundary merge. AOI up to ~12 km across.

start.description: Season start YYYY-MM-DD (default: 12 months before end).

limitations: Sentinel-2 10 m: reliable down to about 0.5-1 ha; adjacent same-crop fields with no visible boundary merge.
Labels describe seasonal behaviour (winter, summer, double-cropped, perennial, fallow); it does not identify crop species.
AOI up to about 12 km across.
operations.confidence: per-field 0-1 score from boundary contrast and NDVI-profile consistency; low for small or merged fields.

operations.name: map_flood
operations.description: Map a FLOOD from Sentinel-1 radar: what went under water, and what was hit. Radar sees through monsoon cloud and gives the sharpest water boundary in remote sensing (open water is dark, smooth backscatter). With `before` and `after` dates it compares the Sentinel-1 RTC scene nearest each (same relative orbit where possible). With only a `start`/`end` window it scans every scene over the AOI, reports the water fraction per scene, takes the peak-water scene as the flood and the nearest earlier dry scene as the reference, and says how it chose. Water = VV dB, 3x3 median, Otsu threshold clamped to -23..-15 dB (fallback -18 dB, stated), flood = water(after) AND NOT water(before). Returns new-flood and permanent-water polygons (km²), receded water, Overture buildings whose footprint centroid is inside the flood (count + map layer), flooded road length, both SAR scenes as map layers, and a water-fraction-by-scene chart. Use for "flood", "inundation", "what went under water", "how much flooded", "which buildings were hit". Honest limits: misses flooding under vegetation and in dense urban areas (double bounce), wind-roughened water, no terrain-shadow mask. AOI up to ~40 km across.

before.description: YYYY-MM-DD of the dry reference; the nearest Sentinel-1 scene is used. Give together with `after`.

after.description: YYYY-MM-DD during/after the flood; the nearest Sentinel-1 scene is used.

start.description: Window start YYYY-MM-DD to scan when no explicit dates are given (default: 120 days before `end`).

polarization.description: Radar polarisation (default VV, the better water/land contrast).

min_area_m2.description: Drop flood polygons smaller than this (default 1000 m²).

include_roads.description: Also measure flooded road length from Overture (default true).

limitations: Radar misses flooding under vegetation and in dense urban areas (double bounce), so flooded area and buildings hit are lower bounds.
Wind-roughened water reads as land and there is no terrain-shadow mask.
The water threshold is Otsu clamped to -23..-15 dB (fallback -18 dB, stated in the output), not calibrated to the site.
AOI up to about 40 km across; a scene scan can take about two minutes.
operations.confidence: medium: a real two-scene radar comparison; the output states which scenes were chosen and why.

operations.name: digitize_features
operations.description: One-shot tool to digitize ANY geographic feature into vectors, CV-FIRST. The imagery answers the question and OpenStreetMap is used as a cross-check, not as the answer: (1) water features are measured spectrally with Sentinel-2 NDWI; (2) everything else goes through detect_objects (target profiler -> imagery planner -> detector ladder); (3) OSM is then queried and reported alongside, so the user can see how the imagery result compares with what is already mapped. Use whenever the user asks to "digitize", "find all", "extract", "delineate", "map out", or "show me the X". Prefer this over calling query_osm + detect_objects separately.

feature.description: The feature to digitize (e.g. "lakes", "buildings", "cars", "solar panels"). Supports plurals and synonyms.

footprint_m.description: Optional [long, short] size of ONE such feature in metres. Supply your own estimate for unusual features so the pipeline can judge whether imagery resolves them.

limitations: Floods route to map_flood, fields to delineate_fields and water to a Sentinel-2 NDWI threshold with an OSM cross-check; these are measured, not detected.
Any other object (cars, buildings, tanks) needs the computer-vision pipeline, which is off unless GEOAGENT_ENABLE_CV=1; otherwise the request is refused.
operations.confidence: inherits the routed operation's confidence.

operations.name: make_chart
operations.description: Draw ANY chart (time series, histogram, scatter, bar, spectral profile, correlation matrix, small multiples) as a Vega-Lite spec over data from this session's tool results. Reference data BY NAME, never type values: {"data": {"name": "<result_id>#<summary_key>"}} for a figure listed in a [citation_id: …] hint (arrays become rows {label, value[, date]}), or {"data": {"name": "<result_id>#features"}} for the feature properties of that result's layer (one row per feature, plus `_fid`). Inline `data.values`, `url` and `datasets` are rejected. Unknown names return an error listing the available ones.

spec.description: Vega-Lite spec as a JSON-encoded string: mark, encoding, transform, layer… with `data` given only as {"name": "<result_id>#<key>"}.

limitations: Charts only data this request's own tool results produced, referenced by name; inline values, urls and datasets are rejected.
It draws what the figures say; it does not add analysis.
operations.confidence: not applicable: a chart repeats the cited figures and carries the confidence of the results it draws.

operations.name: style_layer
operations.description: Colour an EXISTING vector layer's features by one of their properties (data-driven styling) and show a legend: "colour each field by median NDVI", "colour buildings by type". Pass `layer_id` (from a [layer_id: …] hint or the Layer Manifest) or `result_id`, and `property`. Numeric property -> graduated classes computed from the data; text property -> categorical. An unknown property returns an error listing the real ones. Does not fetch or compute anything.

layer_id.description: Id of the layer to restyle.

result_id.description: Alternative to layer_id: the result_id whose layer to restyle.

property.description: Feature property to colour by (must exist on the features).

kind.description: Default: graduated for numeric properties, categorical for text.

colormap.description: Ramp: viridis (default), magma, inferno, plasma, cividis, greys, rdylgn, rdbu, spectral, terrain, blues, ylgn (append _r to reverse).

method.description: Graduated class breaks: quantile (default) or equal interval.

classes.description: Categorical only: explicit value -> colour mapping.

limitations: Restyles an existing vector layer; it fetches and computes nothing.
Graduated classes are computed from the layer's own values; an unknown property is refused with the real ones listed.
operations.confidence: not applicable: styling does not change the data; the layer keeps the confidence of the result that made it.

operations.name: find_dataset
operations.description: Search the offline dataset registry: about 16,000 public geospatial datasets from Microsoft Planetary Computer, Google Earth Engine, NASA CMR (cloud-hosted collections), Copernicus Data Space, Element 84, EODC, Global Forest Watch, OpenTopography lidar surveys, plus curated APIs (Overture Maps, OpenStreetMap, Open-Meteo, SoilGrids, WorldPop, FIRMS, GIBS, USGS 3DEP lidar, ARCO-ERA5, building footprints). Instant and key-free. Ranks by relevance to your plain-words request and keeps only datasets whose declared extent covers the AOI (global ones always pass). Returns the top 5-8 with id, themes, resolution, temporal range, coverage verdict, licence, access kind and whether credentials are needed. Falls back to a live STAC catalog search only when the registry has no good hit, and returns nothing rather than a weak guess. Use when the user asks for data no existing tool measures (biomass, soil moisture, burned area, lidar, SAR, DEMs, population, night lights, air quality, climate reanalysis...). Follow up with use_dataset({dataset_id}) to read a hit; its line says what the read will do or what is missing.

query.description: What kind of data, in plain words: "soil moisture", "deforestation alerts", "30 m DEM", "SAR backscatter", "population density".

themes.description: Optional hard filter, any of: elevation, lidar, sar, optical, land-cover, vegetation, forest, agriculture, soil, climate, weather, precipitation, temperature, water, hydrology, snow-ice, ocean, air-quality, fire, population, urban, buildings, infrastructure, nightlights, geology, biodiversity, hazards, boundaries, embeddings.

max_resolution_m.description: Optional: only datasets at least this fine (metres). Datasets with unstated resolution still pass.

start.description: Optional start of the period of interest (YYYY or YYYY-MM-DD).

end.description: Optional end of the period of interest (YYYY or YYYY-MM-DD).

license.description: Optional comma-separated licence ids, or "open" for any open licence (CC-BY, CC0, ODbL, public domain...).

live.description: Skip the registry and search live STAC catalogs instead (slow; for brand-new collections).

breadth.description: Live fallback only: also query the STAC Index registry beyond the three main catalogs (default true).

limitations: Searches an offline snapshot of about 16,000 public datasets; its coverage verdict uses each dataset's declared extent, which is not proof of data over the AOI.
A hit marked not readable cannot be computed on in this app; it is a pointer, not data.
operations.confidence: relevance ranking only; it says nothing about data quality.

operations.name: use_dataset
operations.description: Read a dataset found by find_dataset over the drawn AOI: real statistics plus a map layer, through one path for every access kind. Pass the exact `dataset_id` that find_dataset printed. Cloud-optimised rasters (any STAC API) are searched over the AOI/time, the item closest to `date` is chosen (clearest scene for optical), signed if the host needs it, and statistics are computed with the AOI polygon as a cutline (never a bbox); Sentinel-1 / PALSAR SAR is converted to dB, DEMs report metres (add hillshade), categorical data reports class names the collection declares, USGS 3DEP lidar gives surface/terrain/height rasters (point clouds return metadata only). Also reads Earth Engine assets (when credentials exist), Overture Maps buildings/places/roads as a vector layer, and routes curated REST sources (Open-Meteo, SoilGrids, WorldPop, FIRMS, night lights) to their dedicated tools. When a dataset cannot be read it says exactly why (missing NASA Earthdata/Copernicus/OpenTopography/Earth Engine credential, needs the Python Zarr service or openEO account, outside coverage, no items over the AOI): relay that, never substitute numbers. The older `catalog` + `collection` form still works for STAC collections.

dataset_id.description: Registry id exactly as returned by find_dataset, e.g. "planetary-computer:sentinel-1-rtc", "overture:buildings".

variable.description: Optional band / asset / variable: "vv", "vh", "NDVI", "occurrence", "building height". Omit for the primary data asset (the answer names the others).

date.description: Optional target date (YYYY-MM-DD): the acquisition closest to it is used.

start.description: Optional start of a period (YYYY or YYYY-MM-DD).

end.description: Optional end of a period (YYYY or YYYY-MM-DD).

hillshade.description: DEMs: also add a hillshade layer.

collection.description: Legacy: STAC collection id (use with catalog) when no dataset_id is available.

catalog.description: Legacy: catalog id ("planetary-computer", "element84", "landsatlook") or a STAC API root URL. Defaults to planetary-computer.

datetime.description: Legacy: RFC-3339 instant or interval to restrict the item search.

limitations: A discovered dataset is not vetted like a wired tool: units and conventions are the publisher's.
Missing credentials, a Zarr store or an openEO back end make a dataset unreadable; the tool says exactly why and never substitutes numbers.
"No items over this AOI" means the dataset has no data here, not that the value is zero.
operations.confidence: as stated by the data source and the access route used; the output carries its licence and caveats.
